audit_findings.title: Owner earnings may undercharge maintenance investment, including finance-leased assets
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed fiscal-2025 amounts were $118.643 million of property-and-equipment purchases, $18.606 million of new finance-lease assets and $3.958 million of finance-lease principal, versus the $23.9 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring maintenance investment omitted from cash capex, including replacement stores, recurring technology and processing assets acquired through finance leases, should reduce OE and every scenario's operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: Net cash used in investing activities was $118.5 million for fiscal 2025, which consisted primarily of $118.6 million of expenditures related to investments in new stores, offsite processing and information technology, as well as capital maintenance expenditures.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved classification issue, not a demonstrated OE error, because the filing does not separate maintenance from growth investment and the OE bridge was not supplied. It is nevertheless material: the relevant filed investment pools are large relative to the $23.9 million anchor, so a modest reclassification could substantially reduce modeled OE.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $23.9 million anchor to project-level cash capex, store replacements, recurring IT and processing investment, finance-lease additions and finance-lease principal; then rerun all scenarios with the supported maintenance charge.

audit_findings.title: The forecast does not expose the post-hedge interest path
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.3 million of annual interest expense per 100-basis-point rate change, equal to 30.5% of the $23.9 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Interest expense remains in equity-level OE, so changes after the June 2029 swap expiry, scheduled principal amortization and the September 2032 maturity flow directly through projected OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The interest rate swaps are scheduled to mature on June 29, 2029.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual hedge expiry and debt maturity are demonstrated, while future rates and refinancing terms remain uncertain. Because the filed sensitivity equals nearly one-third of anchor OE for each 100-basis-point move, omitting an explicit interest path is reasonably capable of materially changing operating value in either direction.
audit_findings.action: Build and rerun a year-by-year interest schedule through 2032 and the terminal period using filed amortization, swap notionals and expiries, plus separately disclosed refinancing-rate and fee sensitivities.

audit_findings.title: The full cash add-back may include required operating liquidity
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $91.869 million, or $0.54 per fully diluted share; the add-back equals 21.5% of the $428 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash and short-term investments directly to equity value; any amount required for operations, obligations, covenants or subsidiary liquidity is not excess cash and must be removed from that add-back.
audit_findings.evidence: Our primary short-term requirements for liquidity and capital are to meet general working capital needs, fund capital expenditures and make required minimum principal and interest payments on our debt.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding the entire $91.869 million balance is demonstrated, but the amount that is non-distributable is unresolved. The full add-back is large enough relative to base equity value to be material, although removing it would reinforce rather than reverse the conclusion that modeled value is below the $10.45 market price.
audit_findings.action: Establish minimum operating cash by geography and season, identify restricted or trapped balances and covenant requirements, reconcile current liabilities, and rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: A large refinancing loss could distort the recurring anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $35.728 million pre-tax loss, including at least $20.884 million of filed cash prepayment premiums, versus the $23.9 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining a nonrecurring extinguishment loss depresses OE, while excluding cash premiums and recurring refinancing friction can inflate OE; debt-issuance amortization also affects the continuing interest charge.
audit_findings.evidence: Net income was $22.6 million, or $0.14 per diluted share, which included a $35.7 million pre-tax loss on extinguishment of debt.
audit_findings.explanation: The refinancing loss and its cash components are demonstrated, but the supplied OE bridge does not establish their treatment. The gross loss is 149.5% of anchor OE and the filed cash premiums are 87.4%, so either mechanical retention or wholesale removal could materially distort value.
audit_findings.action: Trace each extinguishment charge in the anchor period into cash premiums, noncash write-offs, issuance fees and recurring amortization; normalize only supported nonrecurring amounts and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: A debt-related foreign-exchange gain may be embedded in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified OE adjustment; filed fiscal-2025 amounts were a $14.215 million remeasurement gain, a $3.183 million derivative loss and an $11.032 million net foreign-currency gain, with the net gain equal to 46.2% of the $23.9 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: An unrealized debt-remeasurement gain included in the anchor raises OE and operating value, while realized hedge cash flows and continuing hedge costs should be treated consistently rather than removed indiscriminately.
audit_findings.evidence: In fiscal 2025, the USD weakened against the CAD relative to December 28, 2024, which resulted in remeasurement gains of $14.2 million primarily from USD-denominated debt held by one of our Canadian subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The foreign-exchange amounts are demonstrated, but their inclusion in the $23.9 million OE anchor is not established without the bridge. If the net episodic gain was retained, its scale relative to anchor OE makes the resulting overstatement material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile OE to the foreign-currency and derivative lines, separating unrealized debt remeasurement from realized hedge cash flows and ongoing hedge costs; neutralize only nonrecurring noncash movements and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: The growth ruling mistakes fiscal 2025 for a missing year and ignores a 53rd week
audit_findings.magnitude: A mechanical 52-week normalization gives $23.45 million of OE, $0.45 million or 1.9% below the $23.9 million anchor; applied proportionally, base operating value falls about $6.3 million, or approximately $0.04 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Correct fiscal-year spacing affects the qualitative growth ruling, while removing the extra week reduces the latest OE anchor and therefore operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: Our last three fiscal years consisted of the 53 weeks ended January 3, 2026 (“fiscal 2025”), the 52 weeks ended December 28, 2024 (“fiscal 2024”) and the 52 weeks ended December 30, 2023 (“fiscal 2023”).
audit_findings.explanation: The asserted missing year is a demonstrated factual error: fiscal 2023, fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2025 are consecutive observations. Nevertheless, correcting the label does not remove the documented rise from $31.1 million to $60.4 million and reversal to $23.9 million, and the anchor rule already selects the latest result because it is below trend. The mechanical 53rd-week effect is only about 1.9%, far too small to alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Relabel the observations as fiscal 2023-2025, delete the missing-year rationale, calculate a supportable 52-week normalization rather than relying solely on the mechanical estimate, and document whether the corrected chronology changes scenario-growth judgment.
